name: Apogee
description: Lets media buyers, agencies and consultants bulk-upload hundreds of ad creatives in minutes, "the painful workflow Meta's native tools never solved" (founder-stated). Extras: naming-convention enforcement, test structures, Autopilot (cuts losers on Meta), comment analysis, funnel analytics, and an MCP/API bridge (company-stated). Homepage: "Déjà adopté par +300 media buyers, marques et agences", "un lancement se configure en 47 secondes, pour 1 ou 300 créatives", 7-day trial for €1, and an agency workspace with sliding per-consultant pricing on one invoice (company-stated). 30% lifetime affiliate program (founder-stated). Profile founded Feb 2026 (revenue starts at ~$3.2k in Feb, so the business probably existed before; not stated). France, founder Mathieu (832 X followers). 43 subscriptions; L30 margin 80%.

mentions.evidence: MRR $4,099 · 43 active subscriptions Last 30 days $3,587 (+3.6%) · last 3 months $10,240 · last 6 months $18,627 Last 12 months / all-time $26,998 L30 profit margin 80% (TrustMRR snapshot) Monthly: $3,228 (Feb 2026) → $2,753–3,343 (Mar–Aug) → $3,952 (Sep); Oct MTD $1,212. Revenue synced 20 October 2026 ~05:13 Warsaw.
mentions.indieAngle: Same "bulk ops over a hated ad UI" play, but for Allegro Ads, Google Merchant Center feeds, or LinkedIn Campaign Manager. Make the first version Polish-language for local performance agencies, then add an agency seat price.

whyItPrints: It's ops glue for a UI everybody hates (Ads Manager). Agencies launching dozens of creatives a week for many clients are the buyers. It's French-language, which keeps US competitors out, and revenue has been flat-steady ~$3k/month for eight months.
